about: THE source of truth for this site. The site is Airis OS: one Cloudflare Worker serves every file in this repo as a static asset and routes /api/*. Every rule a human or agent needs to add, change or remove an app is in this file. Code reads this file at runtime (shell.js, worker.js via lib/router.js, scripts/dev.mjs, scripts/check.mjs) - when prose elsewhere disagrees, this file wins.

addApp: 1. Write the app as ONE self-contained HTML file under apps/<id>.html (inline CSS/JS, no external requests) if it should be installable as code; or keep an existing multi-file page where it is and use install:'link'.
2. Append one entry to manifest.json .apps that satisfies appEntry below. id must match appEntry.fields.id.pattern and be unique.
3. If it needs storage, secrets, network, OS actions or the store, list them in capabilities and talk to the shell over the bridge (see bridge). Never add allow-same-origin.
4. If the page forbids framing (frame-ancestors) or needs real origin storage (localStorage/IndexedDB of its own), set launch:'standalone'.
5. Run: node scripts/check.mjs   (validates manifest + files + CSP + routes against this contract).
6. Run: node scripts/dev.mjs   and open http://localhost:8788/#app/<id>.
changeApp: Edit the file. For install:'code' apps also bump the entry's version in manifest.json - catalogue-installed records auto-update when the manifest version differs; imported records are never overwritten.
removeApp: Delete the entry from manifest.json (browsers keep an installed copy until the user uninstalls it; catalogue records whose entry vanished are shown as orphaned in Store).
If the file had a public URL, keep the file or add a redirect in worker.redirects so the old URL does not break.
recipes.addProviderPreset: Append one object to manifest.json -> apps[id=session].settings.presets matching sessionPreset below. No code change.
recipes.addUpstream: Add one key to worker.upstreams. It is served at /api/<key>/<allowed path>. No code change.

layout.index.html: the OS shell page (served at /). Terminal floor markup first, OS chrome hidden until boot succeeds.
layout.terminal.js / terminal.css: the floor. No dependency on shell, manifest, contract, storage or network. Must keep working if everything else fails.
layout.shell.js / shell.css: window manager, bridge host, action registry, event trail, install records. Reads manifest.json and this file.
layout.manifest.json: the app catalogue, never the PWA manifest. What exists. Not what runs - an install record is what runs.
layout.site.webmanifest: the PWA manifest for the shell and home screen.
layout.apps/: first-party apps (session, store, persona, todo, desk, house). apps/<id>.html.
layout.worker.js: Worker entry. Thin: imports this file and lib/router.js.
layout.lib/router.js: route table implementation shared by worker.js and scripts/dev.mjs (pure fetch API, no Worker or Node specifics). Server-side only: listed in .assetsignore, never served.
layout.wrangler.jsonc: Worker config. assets.directory = '.' (the repo root IS the site).
layout.scripts/dev.mjs: dependency-free Node dev server: static files + same router. node scripts/dev.mjs [port]
layout.AGENTS.md: pointer to this file for agents that look there first; holds no rules.
layout.*.html at root, art/: pre-existing standalone pages. Their URLs are permanent (see tests.legacyUrls).

pwa.height: html/body use 100vh, never 100% (iOS falls back to non-cover layout) or 100dvh (PWA cold-start values are wrong until rotation).
pwa.insets: JS probes safe-area insets into --sat/--sar/--sab/--sal at 0/100/500/1000ms, on resize and orientationchange, and toggles viewport-fit on standalone cold start; the CSS env() variable bridge is unreliable.
pwa.landscape: Touch landscape has an unreported top dead zone; use max(20px, safe-area-inset-top) as the floor, and inset the desktop stage and taskbar.
pwa.zoom: Keep pinch zoom: no maximum-scale or user-scalable=no; use touch-action: manipulation on shell chrome instead.

id.doc: stable key; also the #app/<id> deep link and the storage namespace

title.doc: optional window title; defaults to name

url.doc: root-relative path (no leading slash, no ../) or absolute https URL. For install:'code' this is where the code is fetched from at install time.

install.doc: code: the HTML is fetched and stored in the install record and runs from there (srcdoc). link: the record stores only the URL and the page runs from the URL.

preinstalled.doc: installed automatically on first boot and kept up to date from the catalogue

launch.doc: auto: sandboxed window (desktop) / sheet (phone). standalone: new browser tab, no frame.

hidden.doc: not on the desktop grid; still in terminal ls, Store, and #app/<id>

capabilities.doc: bridge ops the app may call; anything not listed is refused

settings.doc: free-form data handed to the app in the bridge hello reply (e.g. Session presets)

legacyUrls.doc: old public URLs of this app; each must resolve (file or redirect)

rules: install:'code' requires url to be a local .html file and launch:'auto'.
launch:'standalone' apps get no bridge (they are not framed).
An external https url must use launch:'standalone' or install:'link'.

appFiles.codeApps: Single HTML file. Everything inline. It runs as <iframe srcdoc> with an opaque origin, so it has NO localStorage, cookies, IndexedDB or same-origin fetch of its own - use the bridge. Relative URLs resolve against the shell page (site root).
appFiles.linkApps: Any page. It runs as <iframe src=url> with an opaque origin (same limits) unless launch:'standalone'.
appFiles.theme: The hello reply carries theme:'dark'|'light'. The shell also posts {airis:1, event:'theme', theme} on change.

sandbox.why: Opaque origin: an app cannot touch the shell DOM, the shell's localStorage (where keys and install records live), or another app. All privilege goes through the bridge, which checks capabilities and writes the trail.

csp.shell: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; media-src 'self' data:; frame-src 'self' https://lexfall.com; connect-src 'self' https: http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*; font-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'
csp.where: index.html <meta http-equiv=Content-Security-Policy>. srcdoc code apps inherit it.

why.script-src 'unsafe-inline': code apps are single inline files running under the inherited policy
why.connect-src https: localhost: the shell performs net.stream for apps: same-origin /api/go, or a user-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenRouter over https, LM Studio on localhost)
why.img-src blob:: Store export builds a Blob download URL
why.frame-src lexfall.com: kept for compatibility; Lexfall itself launches standalone because it sends frame-ancestors 'none'

csp.apiHeaders: Worker /api responses carry cache-control: no-store and never set-cookie.

bridge.transport: window.postMessage between the app frame and the shell. The shell identifies the caller by event.source (the frame's contentWindow), never by anything the app claims.

trail.note.doc: app writes one line to the shared trail as actor app:<id>

secret.has.doc: there is deliberately no secret.get: the value never returns to app code

net.stream.args: { url, method, headers, body, auth: { secret, scheme, header } }
net.stream.doc: shell fetches; streams text chunks; final reply value { status, statusText, contentType, text? }. auth header defaults to 'Authorization': its value is '<scheme default Bearer> <secret>'; for another header (e.g. 'x-api-key') it is '[<scheme> ]<secret>'. Caller-supplied authorization and headers matching the auth header are dropped. The value comes only from this app's secret store and only goes to this call's url.

os.do.doc: runs a registered action whose agent flag is true; actor is logged as agent:<app id>

actions.doc: One registry. Pointer UI, the Summon palette, the terminal (when the shell is up), window.airis.do() for a browser-driving agent, and the Session agent's tool calls all dispatch through it. Every dispatch lands in the trail with its actor.

note.doc: write a line to the trail

storage.where: browser localStorage of the site origin only. Nothing is stored server-side; the Worker has no KV, D1, R2 or Durable Object bindings.

keys.airis.trail.v1: array of trailEvent, newest last, capped at trail.max
keys.airis.secret.<id>.<name>: app secret (bridge secret.*). Never exported, never shown in state or trail.

event.detail: short string; never contains secret values, request headers or bodies

shape.version: from the entry at install time
shape.entry: copy of the manifest entry (capabilities and settings included)
shape.code: full HTML string when entry.install is 'code', else null

rules: The record is what runs: code records run as srcdoc=record.code; link records run from record.entry.url.
source:'catalogue' records are refreshed when manifest version differs. source:'import' records are never overwritten by the catalogue.
preinstalled catalogue entries are installed on boot if missing (unless the user uninstalled them: id is kept in removed[]).

bundle.excludes: secrets, app storage, trail, window layout
bundle.import: each record is validated against installRecord + appEntry. A record identical to the installed one (version, entry, code) is left untouched. Other valid ones are stored with source:'import' (replacing same id; an open window of that app restarts). Invalid ones are reported and skipped.

fields.label: string shown in the strip
fields.transport: 'proxy' | 'direct'. proxy: the provider refuses browser CORS, so the browser calls this site's same-origin relay. baseUrl must be exactly /api/<name> for a key <name> of worker.upstreams, editable must be false, and the strip shows no Base URL box. direct: the provider allows browser CORS; baseUrl is the provider's own absolute http(s) base, never under /api/; editable is true only for the user's own custom endpoint. Adding a direct preset needs no Worker change; adding a proxy preset needs a worker.upstreams entry first.
fields.baseUrl: the URL the app actually calls: <baseUrl>/chat/completions and <baseUrl>/models. proxy: /api/go (our route, not the provider's API). direct: e.g. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 or http://localhost:1234/v1.
fields.upstream: proxy only, required: the real provider base, never rendered in the UI. Must equal worker.upstreams[<name>].base so the label never lies about where the relay goes.
fields.note: optional maintainer note on a proxy preset (why its endpoint is fixed); never rendered in the UI
fields.model: NOT a preset field: presets carry no model and there is no default. The user types the model id in the strip (the GET <baseUrl>/models list is only a suggestion datalist and never auto-fills it); it is stored per preset in this browser only, via storage.set key 'settings' (site-origin localStorage), and never stored by the Worker. Sending is refused until it is filled in.
fields.hint: optional plain-language line shown beside a named (non-editable) preset, e.g. "Relayed by this site — no setup needed". Must contain no URL, hostname or path; check.mjs enforces it. The strip never renders baseUrl, upstream or note for a named preset.
fields.editable: boolean: true only for the custom preset, whose Base URL box is the only place the strip shows an address; false presets ignore any saved base override
fields.headers: optional extra request headers; the literal {session} is replaced with the conversation id. The key goes only through net.stream auth, which the shell attaches from the secret store: Anthropic dialect uses raw x-api-key; OpenAI/chat-completions uses Authorization Bearer. Every direct Anthropic request also sends anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true; proxy and OpenAI requests never send it.

why.doc: Measured 2026-11-14 with Origin: https://jaxah.com. Re-measure before changing a preset's transport; check.mjs enforces the shape.
why.opencode-go: proxy. OPTIONS /chat/completions on https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1 and on https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1 -> HTTP 404 with no access-control-* headers, so every browser blocks a direct call. GET /models and POST /chat/completions themselves answer 200 server-side (the latter only with an x-opencode-session header; without it: 400 MissingSessionID). Pointing the app at opencode.ai directly breaks Session in every browser; /api/go is load-bearing.
why.openrouter: direct. OPTIONS https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions -> HTTP 204 with access-control-allow-origin: * and Authorization in access-control-allow-headers. No Worker route, no session header; the key travels only browser -> openrouter.ai.

routes.doc: same-origin passthrough. Only (method, path) pairs in that upstream's allow list. Anything else under /api: 404 JSON. Wrong method: 405. Cross-origin Origin header: 403. Query strings dropped.
only reached when no static asset matches

routes.to: static asset from the repo root (assets.directory '.', html_handling auto-trailing-slash: /page.html 307s to /page which serves page.html - same as Pages did)

requireHeader.name: x-opencode-session
requireHeader.ifMissing: random uuid per request (send a stable one per conversation instead; Session does)

worker.keyHandling: Authorization is copied from the caller to the upstream and nowhere else: not logged, not stored, not echoed in errors. The Worker has no storage bindings.

dev.wrangler: npx wrangler dev        # http://localhost:8787 (needs wrangler; nothing to npm install in this repo)
dev.node: node scripts/dev.mjs       # http://localhost:8788 - static + the same lib/router.js; no dependencies
dev.stubUpstream: UPSTREAM_GO=http://127.0.0.1:9999 node scripts/dev.mjs   # point /api/go at a local stub

tests.unit: node --test lib/*.test.mjs   # registry + agent loop, no network, no key
tests.live: node scripts/check.mjs --live http://localhost:8788  # also: every legacy URL resolves, /api allowlist refuses the rest
